title and abstract.summary: The study measured beetle body length, eye length, antenna length, body width, and roundness in saproxylic beetle communities across different forest ages in the southeastern United States.

methods.summary: The study measured forest composition and landscape forest cover across 40 forested sites varying in forest age and landscape forest cover gradient.

results.summary: The study measured the relationship between various species traits (such as body length, body roundness, eye length, antennal length, body width) and species occurrence in relation to forest characteristics (like forest age, LFC, and deadwood volume) across many species.

discussion.summary: The study investigated how forest age, landscape forest cover, and deadwood amount filtered saproxylic beetles in the Piedmont region of the southeastern United States, focusing on the relationship between morphological traits and species distribution.
